reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) supports the formation of Ti-Zn intermetallics as corrosion barriers in Mg alloys and the ability of ball milling/SPS to produce refined microstructures, but it does not provide specific evidence that the spatial distribution, morphology, and size of these phases critically determine corrosion performance, nor does it confirm that these phases enhance high-temperature oxidation resistance.
premises: Ti and Zn additions to Mg promote intermetallic phases (e.g., Ti2Zn, TiZn16) that act as corrosion barriers
These intermetallic phases provide a shielding effect and limit corrosion front progression
The spatial distribution, morphology, and size of intermetallics critically determine overall corrosion performance
High-energy ball milling and spark plasma sintering can produce bulk Mg-Ti-Zn alloys with refined, non-equilibrium microstructures
Such processing routes can extend solid solubility and maintain nanocrystalline phases, contributing to enhanced corrosion resistance
